As for al-Lat, it belonged to Thaqif; as for al-Uzza, it belonged to Sulaym, Ghatafan, Khath'am, Nasr and Sa'id ibn Bakr; as for Manat, it belonged to Qudayd; as for Asaf, Na'ila and Hubal, they belonged to the people of Makkah. Asaf was opposite the Black Stone, Na'ila was opposite the Yemeni Corner, and Hubal was inside the Ka'bah, eighteen cubits high.

Al-Waqidi said: Wadd was in the form of a man, Suwa' in the form of a woman, Yaghuth in the form of a lion, Ya'uq in the form of a horse, and Nasr in the form of a vulture.

He said: "The things diminished as people diminish today, and they remained upon that as long as Allah willed. Then they abandoned the worship of Allah, the Exalted. So Satan came to them and said: 'What is [the matter] with you that you do not worship anything?' They said: 'Whom shall we worship?' He said: 'These are your gods and the gods of your fathers, which you do not see depicted in your places of prayer.'" He said: "So they worshipped them besides Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent Nuh, who called them to the worship of Allah, the Exalted. They said: ﴿Do not leave your gods﴾ up to His saying, the Exalted and Most High: ﴿and Nasr.﴾"

Sufyan narrated from Musa, from Muhammad ibn Qays, regarding ﴿Do not leave Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq, nor Nasr﴾: "They were righteous people between Adam and Nuh (peace be upon them both), and they had followers who emulated them. When they died, their companions who used to emulate them said: 'If we made their images, it would be more stirring for us toward worship when we remember them.' So they made their images. When they died and others came, Iblis crept up to them and said: 'They only worshipped them, and by them rain was sent down,' so they worshipped them."

Ibn Abbas said: "Nuh used to guard the body of Adam on a mountain in India, preventing the disbelievers from circumambulating his grave. Satan said to them: 'These people boast over you, claiming that they are the children of Adam rather than you, and it is only a body. I will fashion for you its likeness, and you may circumambulate it.' So he carved five idols and led them to worship them: they are Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr. When the time of the drowning came, the Flood buried those idols and covered them with dust, and they remained buried until Satan brought them out for the polytheists of the Arabs. The tribe of Qudha'ah took Wadd and worshipped it at Dumat al-Jandal. Then his elder descendants inherited it, generation after generation, until it came to Kalb, and when Islam came it was still with them. Yaghuth belonged to Tayy, and they took it to Murad and worshipped it for a time. Then the Banu Nājiyah wanted to remove it from A'lā and Anʻam, so they fled with it to al-Husayn, brother of the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b. As for Ya'uq, it belonged to Kahlan, and then his elder descendants inherited it, generation after generation, until it came to Hamdan. As for Nasr, it belonged to Khath'am, who worshipped it. Ibn Kaysan: "What is [the matter] with you that you do not hope, in worshipping Allah, that He will reward you for your reverence of Him with good." Al-Hasan: "You do not know the right of Allah nor thank Him for His blessing." Sa'id ibn Jubayr also said: "They do not hope for Allah's reward nor fear His punishment." And hope (raja') is one of the words with opposite meanings: it can mean expectation and it can mean fear.

﴿And He has created you in stages (atwaran)?﴾ That is, in successive times and states, one after another: a drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, until the completion of creation. ﴿Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens in layers (tibaqan), and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp?﴾ Al-Hasan said: "That is, in the lowest heaven. This is permissible in Arabic speech, as one says: 'I came to the Banu Tamim and some of them came to me,' and says: 'So-and-so is hidden in the houses of the Banu So-and-so,' when in fact it is in one house." Muqatil said: "Its meaning is: and made the moon with them a light for the people of the earth" (fi in the sense of ma'a, "with"). Abdullah ibn Muhammad said: "The sun and the moon, their faces are toward the heavens, and the light of the sun and the radiance of the moon come from them, and their backs are toward the earth. I recite a verse of the Book of Allah, the Exalted, to that effect: ﴿and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp﴾," a shining lamp.

It was said to Abdullah ibn Umar: "What is the matter with the sun, that it warms us at times and cools us at other times?" He said: "In summer it is in the fourth heaven, and in winter it is in the seventh heaven, near the Throne of the Most Merciful. Had it been in the lowest heaven, nothing could stand before it."

﴿And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth as a growth (nabatan).﴾ The original form should have been "inbatan," but it is a verbal noun differing from its root; al-Khalil said: its implied meaning is "you grew, a growing." ﴿Then He will return you into it, and bring you out [again] in a [final] bringing forth (ikhraja).﴾ ﴿And Allah has made for you the earth a spread-out carpet (bisata), a cradle (mihadan), that carries you and covers you when dead, ﴿that you may traverse therein roads, wide paths (fijajan)﴾, different ways.

﴿Nuh said: "My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children increase him in nothing but loss,"﴾ and they are the leaders and the nobles. ﴿And they have plotted a great plot (kubbaran),﴾ great and immense. It is said: "kibar" and "kabbar" (with shadda), both with the same meaning, and similar to this in Arabic speech: "amr 'ajib," "'ujab," and "'ujjab"; "rajul hassan" and "hassan"; "kamal" and "kammal"; "qurra'" for "qari'" and "wudda'" for "wadi'." Ibn al-Sikkit recited:

"A fair one who hunts hearts and captivates, and with beauty turns the heart of the Muslim into a reader (qurra')."

And another said:

"And the man is reached by two remnants of generosity: the nature of the noble and not being wudda' (ornamented/clean)."

Ibn Muhays and Isa read "kubaran" with light stress. They differed concerning the meaning of their plot.

Ibn Abbas said: "They said a great saying." Al-Hasan: "They plotted against the religion of Allah and its people, a great plot."

Al-Dahhak: "They invented lies against Allah and denied His messengers." It was also said: "They incited their lower ones (asfalatahum) to kill Nuh."

﴿And they said: "Do not leave your gods, and do not leave Wadd,"﴾ the people of Madinah read it with a damma on the waw, and others with a fatha, and both are dialects; ﴿nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq,﴾ the common reading leaves these two undeclined; Abu Hatim said: because they are on the pattern of a present-tense verb, and they are also foreign names. Al-A'mash and Ashhab al-Aqili read: "wa-la Yaghutha wa-Ya'uqa" (declined).

Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Baghawi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn al-Miqran narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: Adam (peace be upon him) had five sons: Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr. They were worshippers, and when one of them died they grieved over him with severe grief. Then Satan came to them and said: "Shall I fashion for you an image of him in your place of prayer, so that when you look at it you will remember him?" They said: "We dislike placing anything in our qibla that we pray toward." He said: "Then I will place it at the back of the mosque." They agreed, and he fashioned it for them from brass and lead. Then another died and he fashioned it for them, and then another died and he fashioned it for them. He said: "The things diminished as people diminish today, and they remained upon that as long as Allah willed. Then they abandoned the worship of Allah, the Exalted. So Satan came to them and said: 'What is [the matter] with you that you do not worship anything?' They said: 'Whom shall we worship?' He said: 'These are your gods and the gods of your fathers, which you do not see depicted in your places of prayer.'" He said: "So they worshipped them besides Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent Nuh, who called them to the worship of Allah, the Exalted. They said: ﴿Do not leave your gods﴾ up to His saying, the Exalted and Most High: ﴿and Nasr.﴾"

Sufyan narrated from Musa, from Muhammad ibn Qays, regarding ﴿Do not leave Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq, nor Nasr﴾: "They were righteous people between Adam and Nuh (peace be upon them both), and they had followers who emulated them. When they died, their companions who used to emulate them said: 'If we made their images, it would be more stirring for us toward worship when we remember them.' So they made their images. When they died and others came, Iblis crept up to them and said: 'They only worshipped them, and by them rain was sent down,' so they worshipped them."

Ibn Abbas said: "Nuh used to guard the body of Adam on a mountain in India, preventing the disbelievers from circumambulating his grave. Satan said to them: 'These people boast over you, claiming that they are the children of Adam rather than you, and it is only a body. I will fashion for you its likeness, and you may circumambulate it.' So he carved five idols and led them to worship them: they are Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr. When the time of the drowning came, the Flood buried those idols and covered them with dust, and they remained buried until Satan brought them out for the polytheists of the Arabs. The tribe of Qudha'ah took Wadd and worshipped it at Dumat al-Jandal. Then his elder descendants inherited it, generation after generation, until it came to Kalb, and when Islam came it was still with them. Yaghuth belonged to Tayy, and they took it to Murad and worshipped it for a time. Then the Banu Nājiyah wanted to remove it from A'lā and Anʻam, so they fled with it to al-Husayn, brother of the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b. As for Ya'uq, it belonged to Kahlan, and then his elder descendants inherited it, generation after generation, until it came to Hamdan. As for Nasr, it belonged to Khath'am, who worshipped it. As for Suwa', it belonged to the family of Dhu al-Kala' who worshipped it."

Ata, Qatadah, al-Thumali, and al-Musayyib said: The idols of the people of Nuh passed to the Arabs. Wadd belonged to Kalb at Dumat al-Jandal; Suwa' was at Rahat for Hudhayl; Yaghuth belonged to the Banu Ghutayf of Murad at al-Jawf; Ya'uq belonged to Hamdan; Nasr belonged to the family of Dhu al-Kala' of Himyar. As for al-Lat, it belonged to Thaqif; as for al-Uzza, it belonged to Sulaym, Ghatafan, Khath'am, Nasr and Sa'id ibn Bakr; as for Manat, it belonged to Qudayd; as for Asaf, Na'ila and Hubal, they belonged to the people of Makkah. Asaf was opposite the Black Stone, Na'ila was opposite the Yemeni Corner, and Hubal was inside the Ka'bah, eighteen cubits high.

Al-Waqidi said: Wadd was in the form of a man, Suwa' in the form of a woman, Yaghuth in the form of a lion, Ya'uq in the form of a horse, and Nasr in the form of a vulture.

﴿And they have led many astray (wa-qad adallu kathiran),﴾ that is, by worshipping them and because of them many people went astray. Its parallel is: ﴿My Lord, indeed they have led many of the people astray﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 36.]]. ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error.﴾ ﴿Because of their sins (mimma khati'atihim)﴾, that is, because of their wrongs; "ma" is extra. Abu Amr read "khataya-hum." Abu Hayah and al-A'mash read "mimma khatiatihim" in the singular. ﴿They were drowned and then entered a Fire, and they found for themselves besides Allah no helpers.﴾

Abu Ruq narrated from al-Dahhak regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿They were drowned and then entered a Fire﴾, he said: "That is, in this world, in a single state: they were drowned from one side and burned in the water from another side."

Al-Hasan Abu al-Qasim recited to us, saying: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rimah recited to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari recited to us:

"Creation is sometimes gathered and sometimes scattered, and events are of many kinds and conditions.
Do not be surprised by opposites when they come together, for Allah joins water and fire."

﴿And Nuh said﴾ Muqatil said: "Nuh" in Syriac means "the Quiet One," and he was named Nuh because the earth was quiet with him: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dayyar.﴾ That is, anyone who moves about on the earth, goes and comes. It is a form from "dawran" (turning), like "qiyam," originally "qiwam," and "dayyawar." Al-Qutaybi said: It derives from "dar" (house), meaning one who settles in a dwelling.

﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants﴾. Ibn Abbas said: A man would take his son to Nuh and say: "Beware of this one, for he is a liar, and my father warned me against him." So the elder would die and the younger would grow up upon it.

﴿And they will beget none but wicked, disbelieving [offspring].﴾ That is, those who will disbelieve and transgress. Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Muqatil, al-Rabi', Ata, and Ibn Zayd said: Nuh (peace be upon him) only said this when Allah, the Exalted, had brought forth every believer from their loins and the wombs of their women, and had dried up the loins of their men, forty years before the punishment; it was also said seventy years. And we know that children did not deny the messengers; the punishment fell only upon the deniers.

﴿My Lord, forgive me, and my parents, and whoever enters my house (baytiya) a believer,﴾ that is, my home; al-Dahhak said: my mosque; it was also said: my ship. ﴿And the believing men and believing women,﴾ in general. Al-Kalbi said: from the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction (tabaran)﴾, ruin and perdition.

﴿My Lord, forgive me, and my parents, and whoever enters my house (baytiya) a believer,﴾ that is, my home; al-Dahhak said: my mosque; it was also said: my ship. ﴿And the believing men and believing women,﴾ in general. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Indeed, We sent Nuh to his people, [saying]: "Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment."﴾ He said: "O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner: that you worship Allah, fear Him, and obey me. He will forgive you of your sins" (min is extra, sila) "and defer you to a specified term," which is death, so that He does not destroy you with punishment. "Indeed, the term of Allah, when it comes, is not deferred, if you only knew." He said: "My Lord, indeed I have called my people night and day, but my call has only increased them in flight," (nifaran, meaning fleeing from him) "and indeed, every time I have called them that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears" so that they would not hear my call, "and they covered themselves with their garments," (they covered their faces with them) so that they would not see me and would not hear my voice, "and they persisted in disbelief and acted with arrogant pride. Then indeed I called them openly. Then I announced the call to them publicly, and I spoke to them in private, secretly. And I said: 'Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving. He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain.'"

Al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Abu Ubaydullah al-Makhzumi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us from Mutarrif, from al-Sha'bi: that Umar went out to seek rain for the people, but he did not add anything beyond seeking forgiveness until he returned. They said to him: "We did not see you seek rain (by supplication)." Umar said: "I certainly sought rain from the means of the sky from which rain is sent down," and then he recited: ﴿Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving. He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain.﴾

﴿And He will increase you in wealth and children, and will make for you gardens (bustans) and will make for you rivers flowing.﴾ This is because the people of Nuh, when they denied him for a long time, Allah withheld the rain from them and made the wombs of their women barren for forty years, so their wealth and livestock perished. So Allah promised them that if they believed, He would restore these to them.

And al-Rabi' ibn Subayh narrated that a man came to al-Hasan and complained to him of drought, and al-Hasan said to him: "Seek forgiveness from Allah." Another came to him and complained of poverty, and he said to him: "Seek forgiveness from Allah." Another came to him and said: "Pray to Allah that He grant me a son," and he said to him: "Seek forgiveness from Allah." Another came to him and complained of the drying up of his gardens, and he said to him: "Seek forgiveness from Allah." We said: "Men came to you complaining of different afflictions and asking for various things, and you ordered them all to seek forgiveness?" He said: "I did not say anything of my own accord in this; I only drew a lesson from the words of Allah, the Exalted, relating about His Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) that he said to his people:"

﴿Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving. He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain, and will increase you in wealth and children, and will make for you gardens and will make for you rivers.﴾

﴿What is [the matter] with you that you do not expect for Allah any dignity (waqaran)?﴾ Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: "What is [the matter] with you that you do not see for Allah any greatness." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "What is [the matter] with you that you do not venerate Allah with His due veneration." Mansur, from Mujahid: "You do not care for His greatness."

Al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas: "You do not know for Allah any greatness." Qatadah: "You do not hope for Allah any consequence." Ibn Zayd: "You do not see for Allah any obedience." Al-Kalbi: "You do not fear the greatness of Allah." Ibn Kaysan: "What is [the matter] with you that you do not hope, in worshipping Allah, that He will reward you for your reverence of Him with good." Al-Hasan: "You do not know the right of Allah nor thank Him for His blessing." Sa'id ibn Jubayr also said: "They do not hope for Allah's reward nor fear His punishment." And hope (raja') is one of the words with opposite meanings: it can mean expectation and it can mean fear.

﴿And He has created you in stages (atwaran)?﴾ That is, in successive times and states, one after another: a drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, until the completion of creation. ﴿Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens in layers (tibaqan), and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp?﴾ Al-Hasan said: "That is, in the lowest heaven. Muqatil said: "Its meaning is: and made the moon with them a light for the people of the earth" (fi in the sense of ma'a, "with"). Abdullah ibn Muhammad said: "The sun and the moon, their faces are toward the heavens, and the light of the sun and the radiance of the moon come from them, and their backs are toward the earth. I recite a verse of the Book of Allah, the Exalted, to that effect: ﴿and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp﴾," a shining lamp.

It was said to Abdullah ibn Umar: "What is the matter with the sun, that it warms us at times and cools us at other times?" He said: "In summer it is in the fourth heaven, and in winter it is in the seventh heaven, near the Throne of the Most Merciful. Had it been in the lowest heaven, nothing could stand before it."

﴿And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth as a growth (nabatan).﴾ The original form should have been "inbatan," but it is a verbal noun differing from its root; al-Khalil said: its implied meaning is "you grew, a growing." ﴿Then He will return you into it, and bring you out [again] in a [final] bringing forth (ikhraja).﴾ ﴿And Allah has made for you the earth a spread-out carpet (bisata), a cradle (mihadan), that carries you and covers you when dead, ﴿that you may traverse therein roads, wide paths (fijajan)﴾, different ways.

﴿Nuh said: "My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children increase him in nothing but loss,"﴾ and they are the leaders and the nobles. ﴿And they have plotted a great plot (kubbaran),﴾ great and immense. It is said: "kibar" and "kabbar" (with shadda), both with the same meaning, and similar to this in Arabic speech: "amr 'ajib," "'ujab," and "'ujjab"; "rajul hassan" and "hassan"; "kamal" and "kammal"; "qurra'" for "qari'" and "wudda'" for "wadi'." Ibn al-Sikkit recited:

"A fair one who hunts hearts and captivates, and with beauty turns the heart of the Muslim into a reader (qurra')."

And another said:

"And the man is reached by two remnants of generosity: the nature of the noble and not being wudda' (ornamented/clean)."

Ibn Muhays and Isa read "kubaran" with light stress. They differed concerning the meaning of their plot.

Ibn Abbas said: "They said a great saying." Al-Hasan: "They plotted against the religion of Allah and its people, a great plot."

Al-Dahhak: "They invented lies against Allah and denied His messengers." It was also said: "They incited their lower ones (asfalatahum) to kill Nuh."

﴿And they said: "Do not leave your gods, and do not leave Wadd,"﴾ the people of Madinah read it with a damma on the waw, and others with a fatha, and both are dialects; ﴿nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq,﴾ the common reading leaves these two undeclined; Abu Hatim said: because they are on the pattern of a present-tense verb, and they are also foreign names. Al-A'mash and Ashhab al-Aqili read: "wa-la Yaghutha wa-Ya'uqa" (declined).

Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Baghawi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn al-Miqran narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: Adam (peace be upon him) had five sons: Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr. They were worshippers, and when one of them died they grieved over him with severe grief. Then Satan came to them and said: "Shall I fashion for you an image of him in your place of prayer, so that when you look at it you will remember him?" They said: "We dislike placing anything in our qibla that we pray toward." He said: "Then I will place it at the back of the mosque." They agreed, and he fashioned it for them from brass and lead. Then another died and he fashioned it for them, and then another died and he fashioned it for them. He said: "The things diminished as people diminish today, and they remained upon that as long as Allah willed. Then they abandoned the worship of Allah, the Exalted. So Satan came to them and said: 'What is [the matter] with you that you do not worship anything?' They said: 'Whom shall we worship?' He said: 'These are your gods and the gods of your fathers, which you do not see depicted in your places of prayer.'" He said: "So they worshipped them besides Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent Nuh, who called them to the worship of Allah, the Exalted. They said: ﴿Do not leave your gods﴾ up to His saying, the Exalted and Most High: ﴿and Nasr.﴾"

Sufyan narrated from Musa, from Muhammad ibn Qays, regarding ﴿Do not leave Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq, nor Nasr﴾: "They were righteous people between Adam and Nuh (peace be upon them both), and they had followers who emulated them. When they died, their companions who used to emulate them said: 'If we made their images, it would be more stirring for us toward worship when we remember them.' So they made their images. When they died and others came, Iblis crept up to them and said: 'They only worshipped them, and by them rain was sent down,' so they worshipped them."

Ibn Abbas said: "Nuh used to guard the body of Adam on a mountain in India, preventing the disbelievers from circumambulating his grave. Satan said to them: 'These people boast over you, claiming that they are the children of Adam rather than you, and it is only a body. I will fashion for you its likeness, and you may circumambulate it.' So he carved five idols and led them to worship them: they are Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr. When the time of the drowning came, the Flood buried those idols and covered them with dust, and they remained buried until Satan brought them out for the polytheists of the Arabs. The tribe of Qudha'ah took Wadd and worshipped it at Dumat al-Jandal. Then his elder descendants inherited it, generation after generation, until it came to Kalb, and when Islam came it was still with them. Yaghuth belonged to Tayy, and they took it to Murad and worshipped it for a time. Then the Banu Nājiyah wanted to remove it from A'lā and Anʻam, so they fled with it to al-Husayn, brother of the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b. As for Ya'uq, it belonged to Kahlan, and then his elder descendants inherited it, generation after generation, until it came to Hamdan. As for Nasr, it belonged to Khath'am, who worshipped it. As for Suwa', it belonged to the family of Dhu al-Kala' who worshipped it."

Ata, Qatadah, al-Thumali, and al-Musayyib said: The idols of the people of Nuh passed to the Arabs. Wadd belonged to Kalb at Dumat al-Jandal; Suwa' was at Rahat for Hudhayl; Yaghuth belonged to the Banu Ghutayf of Murad at al-Jawf; Ya'uq belonged to Hamdan; Nasr belonged to the family of Dhu al-Kala' of Himyar. As for al-Lat, it belonged to Thaqif; as for al-Uzza, it belonged to Sulaym, Ghatafan, Khath'am, Nasr and Sa'id ibn Bakr; as for Manat, it belonged to Qudayd; as for Asaf, Na'ila and Hubal, they belonged to the people of Makkah. Asaf was opposite the Black Stone, Na'ila was opposite the Yemeni Corner, and Hubal was inside the Ka'bah, eighteen cubits high.

Al-Waqidi said: Wadd was in the form of a man, Suwa' in the form of a woman, Yaghuth in the form of a lion, Ya'uq in the form of a horse, and Nasr in the form of a vulture.

﴿And they have led many astray (wa-qad adallu kathiran),﴾ that is, by worshipping them and because of them many people went astray. Its parallel is: ﴿My Lord, indeed they have led many of the people astray﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 36.]]. ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error.﴾ ﴿Because of their sins (mimma khati'atihim)﴾, that is, because of their wrongs; "ma" is extra. Abu Amr read "khataya-hum." Abu Hayah and al-A'mash read "mimma khatiatihim" in the singular. ﴿They were drowned and then entered a Fire, and they found for themselves besides Allah no helpers.﴾

Abu Ruq narrated from al-Dahhak regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿They were drowned and then entered a Fire﴾, he said: "That is, in this world, in a single state: they were drowned from one side and burned in the water from another side."

Al-Hasan Abu al-Qasim recited to us, saying: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rimah recited to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari recited to us:

"Creation is sometimes gathered and sometimes scattered, and events are of many kinds and conditions.

﴿And Nuh said﴾ Muqatil said: "Nuh" in Syriac means "the Quiet One," and he was named Nuh because the earth was quiet with him: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dayyar.﴾ That is, anyone who moves about on the earth, goes and comes. It is a form from "dawran" (turning), like "qiyam," originally "qiwam," and "dayyawar." Al-Qutaybi said: It derives from "dar" (house), meaning one who settles in a dwelling.

﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants﴾. Ibn Abbas said: A man would take his son to Nuh and say: "Beware of this one, for he is a liar, and my father warned me against him." So the elder would die and the younger would grow up upon it.

﴿And they will beget none but wicked, disbelieving [offspring].﴾ That is, those who will disbelieve and transgress. Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Muqatil, al-Rabi', Ata, and Ibn Zayd said: Nuh (peace be upon him) only said this when Allah, the Exalted, had brought forth every believer from their loins and the wombs of their women, and had dried up the loins of their men, forty years before the punishment; it was also said seventy years. Allah, the Exalted, informed Nuh that they would not believe and would not beget a believer, so then Nuh prayed against them, and Allah answered his supplication and destroyed them all, and there was no child among them at the time of the punishment.

Abu al-Aliyah and al-Hasan said: Had He destroyed their children along with them, it would have been a punishment from Allah upon them; but Allah destroyed their offspring and children without punishment, and then destroyed them. The proof of this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them﴾ [[Surah al-Furqan: 37.]]. And we know that children did not deny the messengers; the punishment fell only upon the deniers.

﴿My Lord, forgive me, and my parents, and whoever enters my house (baytiya) a believer,﴾ that is, my home; al-Dahhak said: my mosque; it was also said: my ship. ﴿And the believing men and believing women,﴾ in general. When the time of the drowning came, the Flood buried those idols and covered them with dust, and they remained buried until Satan brought them out for the polytheists of the Arabs. The tribe of Qudha'ah took Wadd and worshipped it at Dumat al-Jandal. Then his elder descendants inherited it, generation after generation, until it came to Kalb, and when Islam came it was still with them. Yaghuth belonged to Tayy, and they took it to Murad and worshipped it for a time. Then the Banu Nājiyah wanted to remove it from A'lā and Anʻam, so they fled with it to al-Husayn, brother of the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b. As for Ya'uq, it belonged to Kahlan, and then his elder descendants inherited it, generation after generation, until it came to Hamdan. As for Nasr, it belonged to Khath'am, who worshipped it. As for Suwa', it belonged to the family of Dhu al-Kala' who worshipped it."

Ata, Qatadah, al-Thumali, and al-Musayyib said: The idols of the people of Nuh passed to the Arabs. Wadd belonged to Kalb at Dumat al-Jandal; Suwa' was at Rahat for Hudhayl; Yaghuth belonged to the Banu Ghutayf of Murad at al-Jawf; Ya'uq belonged to Hamdan; Nasr belonged to the family of Dhu al-Kala' of Himyar. As for al-Lat, it belonged to Thaqif; as for al-Uzza, it belonged to Sulaym, Ghatafan, Khath'am, Nasr and Sa'id ibn Bakr; as for Manat, it belonged to Qudayd; as for Asaf, Na'ila and Hubal, they belonged to the people of Makkah. Asaf was opposite the Black Stone, Na'ila was opposite the Yemeni Corner, and Hubal was inside the Ka'bah, eighteen cubits high.

Al-Waqidi said: Wadd was in the form of a man, Suwa' in the form of a woman, Yaghuth in the form of a lion, Ya'uq in the form of a horse, and Nasr in the form of a vulture.

﴿And they have led many astray (wa-qad adallu kathiran),﴾ that is, by worshipping them and because of them many people went astray. Its parallel is: ﴿My Lord, indeed they have led many of the people astray﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 36.]]. ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error.﴾ ﴿Because of their sins (mimma khati'atihim)﴾, that is, because of their wrongs; "ma" is extra. Abu Amr read "khataya-hum." Abu Hayah and al-A'mash read "mimma khatiatihim" in the singular. ﴿They were drowned and then entered a Fire, and they found for themselves besides Allah no helpers.﴾

Abu Ruq narrated from al-Dahhak regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿They were drowned and then entered a Fire﴾, he said: "That is, in this world, in a single state: they were drowned from one side and burned in the water from another side."

Al-Hasan Abu al-Qasim recited to us, saying: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rimah recited to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari recited to us:

﴿And Nuh said﴾ Muqatil said: "Nuh" in Syriac means "the Quiet One," and he was named Nuh because the earth was quiet with him: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dayyar.﴾ That is, anyone who moves about on the earth, goes and comes. He said: "In summer it is in the fourth heaven, and in winter it is in the seventh heaven, near the Throne of the Most Merciful. Had it been in the lowest heaven, nothing could stand before it."

﴿And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth as a growth (nabatan).﴾ The original form should have been "inbatan," but it is a verbal noun differing from its root; al-Khalil said: its implied meaning is "you grew, a growing." ﴿Then He will return you into it, and bring you out [again] in a [final] bringing forth (ikhraja).﴾ ﴿And Allah has made for you the earth a spread-out carpet (bisata), a cradle (mihadan), that carries you and covers you when dead, ﴿that you may traverse therein roads, wide paths (fijajan)﴾, different ways.

﴿Nuh said: "My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children increase him in nothing but loss,"﴾ and they are the leaders and the nobles. ﴿And they have plotted a great plot (kubbaran),﴾ great and immense. It is said: "kibar" and "kabbar" (with shadda), both with the same meaning, and similar to this in Arabic speech: "amr 'ajib," "'ujab," and "'ujjab"; "rajul hassan" and "hassan"; "kamal" and "kammal"; "qurra'" for "qari'" and "wudda'" for "wadi'." Ibn al-Sikkit recited:

"A fair one who hunts hearts and captivates, and with beauty turns the heart of the Muslim into a reader (qurra')."

And another said:

"And the man is reached by two remnants of generosity: the nature of the noble and not being wudda' (ornamented/clean)."

Ibn Muhays and Isa read "kubaran" with light stress. They differed concerning the meaning of their plot.

Ibn Abbas said: "They said a great saying." Al-Hasan: "They plotted against the religion of Allah and its people, a great plot."

Al-Dahhak: "They invented lies against Allah and denied His messengers." It was also said: "They incited their lower ones (asfalatahum) to kill Nuh."

﴿And they said: "Do not leave your gods, and do not leave Wadd,"﴾ the people of Madinah read it with a damma on the waw, and others with a fatha, and both are dialects; ﴿nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq,﴾ the common reading leaves these two undeclined; Abu Hatim said: because they are on the pattern of a present-tense verb, and they are also foreign names. Al-A'mash and Ashhab al-Aqili read: "wa-la Yaghutha wa-Ya'uqa" (declined).

Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Baghawi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn al-Miqran narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: Adam (peace be upon him) had five sons: Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr. They were worshippers, and when one of them died they grieved over him with severe grief. Then Satan came to them and said: "Shall I fashion for you an image of him in your place of prayer, so that when you look at it you will remember him?" They said: "We dislike placing anything in our qibla that we pray toward." He said: "Then I will place it at the back of the mosque." They agreed, and he fashioned it for them from brass and lead. Then another died and he fashioned it for them, and then another died and he fashioned it for them. He said: "The things diminished as people diminish today, and they remained upon that as long as Allah willed. Then they abandoned the worship of Allah, the Exalted. So Satan came to them and said: 'What is [the matter] with you that you do not worship anything?' They said: 'Whom shall we worship?' He said: 'These are your gods and the gods of your fathers, which you do not see depicted in your places of prayer.'" He said: "So they worshipped them besides Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent Nuh, who called them to the worship of Allah, the Exalted. They said: ﴿Do not leave your gods﴾ up to His saying, the Exalted and Most High: ﴿and Nasr.﴾"

Sufyan narrated from Musa, from Muhammad ibn Qays, regarding ﴿Do not leave Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq, nor Nasr﴾: "They were righteous people between Adam and Nuh (peace be upon them both), and they had followers who emulated them. When they died, their companions who used to emulate them said: 'If we made their images, it would be more stirring for us toward worship when we remember them.' So they made their images. When they died and others came, Iblis crept up to them and said: 'They only worshipped them, and by them rain was sent down,' so they worshipped them."

Ibn Abbas said: "Nuh used to guard the body of Adam on a mountain in India, preventing the disbelievers from circumambulating his grave. Satan said to them: 'These people boast over you, claiming that they are the children of Adam rather than you, and it is only a body. I will fashion for you its likeness, and you may circumambulate it.' So he carved five idols and led them to worship them: they are Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr. When the time of the drowning came, the Flood buried those idols and covered them with dust, and they remained buried until Satan brought them out for the polytheists of the Arabs. The tribe of Qudha'ah took Wadd and worshipped it at Dumat al-Jandal. Then his elder descendants inherited it, generation after generation, until it came to Kalb, and when Islam came it was still with them. Yaghuth belonged to Tayy, and they took it to Murad and worshipped it for a time. Then the Banu Nājiyah wanted to remove it from A'lā and Anʻam, so they fled with it to al-Husayn, brother of the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b. As for Ya'uq, it belonged to Kahlan, and then his elder descendants inherited it, generation after generation, until it came to Hamdan. As for Nasr, it belonged to Khath'am, who worshipped it. As for Suwa', it belonged to the family of Dhu al-Kala' who worshipped it."

Ata, Qatadah, al-Thumali, and al-Musayyib said: The idols of the people of Nuh passed to the Arabs. Wadd belonged to Kalb at Dumat al-Jandal; Suwa' was at Rahat for Hudhayl; Yaghuth belonged to the Banu Ghutayf of Murad at al-Jawf; Ya'uq belonged to Hamdan; Nasr belonged to the family of Dhu al-Kala' of Himyar. As for al-Lat, it belonged to Thaqif; as for al-Uzza, it belonged to Sulaym, Ghatafan, Khath'am, Nasr and Sa'id ibn Bakr; as for Manat, it belonged to Qudayd; as for Asaf, Na'ila and Hubal, they belonged to the people of Makkah. Asaf was opposite the Black Stone, Na'ila was opposite the Yemeni Corner, and Hubal was inside the Ka'bah, eighteen cubits high.

Al-Waqidi said: Wadd was in the form of a man, Suwa' in the form of a woman, Yaghuth in the form of a lion, Ya'uq in the form of a horse, and Nasr in the form of a vulture.

﴿And they have led many astray (wa-qad adallu kathiran),﴾ that is, by worshipping them and because of them many people went astray. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Indeed, We sent Nuh to his people, [saying]: "Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment."﴾ He said: "O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner: that you worship Allah, fear Him, and obey me. He will forgive you of your sins" (min is extra, sila) "and defer you to a specified term," which is death, so that He does not destroy you with punishment. "Indeed, the term of Allah, when it comes, is not deferred, if you only knew." He said: "My Lord, indeed I have called my people night and day, but my call has only increased them in flight," (nifaran, meaning fleeing from him) "and indeed, every time I have called them that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears" so that they would not hear my call, "and they covered themselves with their garments," (they covered their faces with them) so that they would not see me and would not hear my voice, "and they persisted in disbelief and acted with arrogant pride. Then indeed I called them openly. Then I announced the call to them publicly, and I spoke to them in private, secretly. And I said: 'Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving. He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain.'"

Al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Abu Ubaydullah al-Makhzumi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us from Mutarrif, from al-Sha'bi: that Umar went out to seek rain for the people, but he did not add anything beyond seeking forgiveness until he returned. They said to him: "We did not see you seek rain (by supplication)." Umar said: "I certainly sought rain from the means of the sky from which rain is sent down," and then he recited: ﴿Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving. He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain.﴾

﴿And He will increase you in wealth and children, and will make for you gardens (bustans) and will make for you rivers flowing.﴾ This is because the people of Nuh, when they denied him for a long time, Allah withheld the rain from them and made the wombs of their women barren for forty years, so their wealth and livestock perished. So Allah promised them that if they believed, He would restore these to them.

And al-Rabi' ibn Subayh narrated that a man came to al-Hasan and complained to him of drought, and al-Hasan said to him: "Seek forgiveness from Allah." Another came to him and complained of poverty, and he said to him: "Seek forgiveness from Allah." Another came to him and said: "Pray to Allah that He grant me a son," and he said to him: "Seek forgiveness from Allah." Another came to him and complained of the drying up of his gardens, and he said to him: "Seek forgiveness from Allah." We said: "Men came to you complaining of different afflictions and asking for various things, and you ordered them all to seek forgiveness?" He said: "I did not say anything of my own accord in this; I only drew a lesson from the words of Allah, the Exalted, relating about His Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) that he said to his people:"

﴿Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving. He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain, and will increase you in wealth and children, and will make for you gardens and will make for you rivers.﴾

﴿What is [the matter] with you that you do not expect for Allah any dignity (waqaran)?﴾ Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: "What is [the matter] with you that you do not see for Allah any greatness." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "What is [the matter] with you that you do not venerate Allah with His due veneration." Mansur, from Mujahid: "You do not care for His greatness."

Al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas: "You do not know for Allah any greatness." Qatadah: "You do not hope for Allah any consequence." Ibn Zayd: "You do not see for Allah any obedience." Al-Kalbi: "You do not fear the greatness of Allah." Ibn Kaysan: "What is [the matter] with you that you do not hope, in worshipping Allah, that He will reward you for your reverence of Him with good." Al-Hasan: "You do not know the right of Allah nor thank Him for His blessing." Sa'id ibn Jubayr also said: "They do not hope for Allah's reward nor fear His punishment." And hope (raja') is one of the words with opposite meanings: it can mean expectation and it can mean fear.

﴿And He has created you in stages (atwaran)?﴾ That is, in successive times and states, one after another: a drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, until the completion of creation. ﴿Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens in layers (tibaqan), and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp?﴾ Al-Hasan said: "That is, in the lowest heaven. This is permissible in Arabic speech, as one says: 'I came to the Banu Tamim and some of them came to me,' and says: 'So-and-so is hidden in the houses of the Banu So-and-so,' when in fact it is in one house." Muqatil said: "Its meaning is: and made the moon with them a light for the people of the earth" (fi in the sense of ma'a, "with"). Abdullah ibn Muhammad said: "The sun and the moon, their faces are toward the heavens, and the light of the sun and the radiance of the moon come from them, and their backs are toward the earth. I recite a verse of the Book of Allah, the Exalted, to that effect: ﴿and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp﴾," a shining lamp.

It was said to Abdullah ibn Umar: "What is the matter with the sun, that it warms us at times and cools us at other times?" He said: "In summer it is in the fourth heaven, and in winter it is in the seventh heaven, near the Throne of the Most Merciful. Had it been in the lowest heaven, nothing could stand before it."

﴿And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth as a growth (nabatan).﴾ The original form should have been "inbatan," but it is a verbal noun differing from its root; al-Khalil said: its implied meaning is "you grew, a growing." ﴿Then He will return you into it, and bring you out [again] in a [final] bringing forth (ikhraja).﴾ ﴿And Allah has made for you the earth a spread-out carpet (bisata), a cradle (mihadan), that carries you and covers you when dead, ﴿that you may traverse therein roads, wide paths (fijajan)﴾, different ways.

﴿Nuh said: "My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children increase him in nothing but loss,"﴾ and they are the leaders and the nobles. ﴿And they have plotted a great plot (kubbaran),﴾ great and immense. It is said: "kibar" and "kabbar" (with shadda), both with the same meaning, and similar to this in Arabic speech: "amr 'ajib," "'ujab," and "'ujjab"; "rajul hassan" and "hassan"; "kamal" and "kammal"; "qurra'" for "qari'" and "wudda'" for "wadi'." Ibn al-Sikkit recited:

"A fair one who hunts hearts and captivates, and with beauty turns the heart of the Muslim into a reader (qurra')."

And another said:

"And the man is reached by two remnants of generosity: the nature of the noble and not being wudda' (ornamented/clean)."

Ibn Muhays and Isa read "kubaran" with light stress. They differed concerning the meaning of their plot.

Ibn Abbas said: "They said a great saying." Al-Hasan: "They plotted against the religion of Allah and its people, a great plot."

Al-Dahhak: "They invented lies against Allah and denied His messengers." It was also said: "They incited their lower ones (asfalatahum) to kill Nuh."

﴿And they said: "Do not leave your gods, and do not leave Wadd,"﴾ the people of Madinah read it with a damma on the waw, and others with a fatha, and both are dialects; ﴿nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq,﴾ the common reading leaves these two undeclined; Abu Hatim said: because they are on the pattern of a present-tense verb, and they are also foreign names. Al-A'mash and Ashhab al-Aqili read: "wa-la Yaghutha wa-Ya'uqa" (declined).

Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Baghawi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn al-Miqran narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us from Yazid ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: Adam (peace be upon him) had five sons: Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr. They were worshippers, and when one of them died they grieved over him with severe grief. Then Satan came to them and said: "Shall I fashion for you an image of him in your place of prayer, so that when you look at it you will remember him?" They said: "We dislike placing anything in our qibla that we pray toward." He said: "Then I will place it at the back of the mosque." They agreed, and he fashioned it for them from brass and lead. Then another died and he fashioned it for them, and then another died and he fashioned it for them. He said: "The things diminished as people diminish today, and they remained upon that as long as Allah willed. Then they abandoned the worship of Allah, the Exalted. So Satan came to them and said: 'What is [the matter] with you that you do not worship anything?' They said: 'Whom shall we worship?' He said: 'These are your gods and the gods of your fathers, which you do not see depicted in your places of prayer.'" He said: "So they worshipped them besides Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent Nuh, who called them to the worship of Allah, the Exalted. They said: ﴿Do not leave your gods﴾ up to His saying, the Exalted and Most High: ﴿and Nasr.﴾"

Sufyan narrated from Musa, from Muhammad ibn Qays, regarding ﴿Do not leave Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq, nor Nasr﴾: "They were righteous people between Adam and Nuh (peace be upon them both), and they had followers who emulated them. When they died, their companions who used to emulate them said: 'If we made their images, it would be more stirring for us toward worship when we remember them.' So they made their images. When they died and others came, Iblis crept up to them and said: 'They only worshipped them, and by them rain was sent down,' so they worshipped them."

Ibn Abbas said: "Nuh used to guard the body of Adam on a mountain in India, preventing the disbelievers from circumambulating his grave. Satan said to them: 'These people boast over you, claiming that they are the children of Adam rather than you, and it is only a body. I will fashion for you its likeness, and you may circumambulate it.' So he carved five idols and led them to worship them: they are Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr. When the time of the drowning came, the Flood buried those idols and covered them with dust, and they remained buried until Satan brought them out for the polytheists of the Arabs. The tribe of Qudha'ah took Wadd and worshipped it at Dumat al-Jandal. Then his elder descendants inherited it, generation after generation, until it came to Kalb, and when Islam came it was still with them. Yaghuth belonged to Tayy, and they took it to Murad and worshipped it for a time. Then the Banu Nājiyah wanted to remove it from A'lā and Anʻam, so they fled with it to al-Husayn, brother of the Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b. As for Ya'uq, it belonged to Kahlan, and then his elder descendants inherited it, generation after generation, until it came to Hamdan. As for Nasr, it belonged to Khath'am, who worshipped it. As for Suwa', it belonged to the family of Dhu al-Kala' who worshipped it."

Ata, Qatadah, al-Thumali, and al-Musayyib said: The idols of the people of Nuh passed to the Arabs. Wadd belonged to Kalb at Dumat al-Jandal; Suwa' was at Rahat for Hudhayl; Yaghuth belonged to the Banu Ghutayf of Murad at al-Jawf; Ya'uq belonged to Hamdan; Nasr belonged to the family of Dhu al-Kala' of Himyar. As for al-Lat, it belonged to Thaqif; as for al-Uzza, it belonged to Sulaym, Ghatafan, Khath'am, Nasr and Sa'id ibn Bakr; as for Manat, it belonged to Qudayd; as for Asaf, Na'ila and Hubal, they belonged to the people of Makkah. Asaf was opposite the Black Stone, Na'ila was opposite the Yemeni Corner, and Hubal was inside the Ka'bah, eighteen cubits high.

Al-Waqidi said: Wadd was in the form of a man, Suwa' in the form of a woman, Yaghuth in the form of a lion, Ya'uq in the form of a horse, and Nasr in the form of a vulture.

﴿And they have led many astray (wa-qad adallu kathiran),﴾ that is, by worshipping them and because of them many people went astray. Its parallel is: ﴿My Lord, indeed they have led many of the people astray﴾ [[Surah Ibrahim: 36.]]. ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error.﴾ ﴿Because of their sins (mimma khati'atihim)﴾, that is, because of their wrongs; "ma" is extra. Abu Amr read "khataya-hum." Abu Hayah and al-A'mash read "mimma khatiatihim" in the singular. ﴿They were drowned and then entered a Fire, and they found for themselves besides Allah no helpers.﴾

Abu Ruq narrated from al-Dahhak regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿They were drowned and then entered a Fire﴾, he said: "That is, in this world, in a single state: they were drowned from one side and burned in the water from another side."

Al-Hasan Abu al-Qasim recited to us, saying: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rimah recited to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari recited to us:

"Creation is sometimes gathered and sometimes scattered, and events are of many kinds and conditions.
Do not be surprised by opposites when they come together, for Allah joins water and fire."

﴿And Nuh said﴾ Muqatil said: "Nuh" in Syriac means "the Quiet One," and he was named Nuh because the earth was quiet with him: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dayyar.﴾ That is, anyone who moves about on the earth, goes and comes. It is a form from "dawran" (turning), like "qiyam," originally "qiwam," and "dayyawar." Al-Qutaybi said: It derives from "dar" (house), meaning one who settles in a dwelling.

﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants﴾. Ibn Abbas said: A man would take his son to Nuh and say: "Beware of this one, for he is a liar, and my father warned me against him." So the elder would die and the younger would grow up upon it.

﴿And they will beget none but wicked, disbelieving [offspring].﴾ That is, those who will disbelieve and transgress. Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Muqatil, al-Rabi', Ata, and Ibn Zayd said: Nuh (peace be upon him) only said this when Allah, the Exalted, had brought forth every believer from their loins and the wombs of their women, and had dried up the loins of their men, forty years before the punishment; it was also said seventy years. Allah, the Exalted, informed Nuh that they would not believe and would not beget a believer, so then Nuh prayed against them, and Allah answered his supplication and destroyed them all, and there was no child among them at the time of the punishment.

Abu al-Aliyah and al-Hasan said: Had He destroyed their children along with them, it would have been a punishment from Allah upon them; but Allah destroyed their offspring and children without punishment, and then destroyed them. The proof of this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the people of Nuh, when they denied the messengers, We drowned them﴾ [[Surah al-Furqan: 37.]]. And we know that children did not deny the messengers; the punishment fell only upon the deniers.

﴿My Lord, forgive me, and my parents, and whoever enters my house (baytiya) a believer,﴾ that is, my home; al-Dahhak said: my mosque; it was also said: my ship. ﴿And the believing men and believing women,﴾ in general. Al-Kalbi said: from the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction (tabaran)﴾, ruin and perdition.
